How to Avoid Survey Bias: 10 Practical Strategies for More Accurate Research
Because bias often enters the research process long before anyone starts analyzing the data.
Survey bias is a systematic error. If your research process consistently pushes results in one direction, a larger sample may simply make the wrong answer look more convincing.
The good news is that you can reduce many common sources of survey bias through better questionnaire design, thoughtful sampling, appropriate data collection methods, and careful quality control.
This guide provides 10 practical strategies for avoiding survey bias, from writing the first question to reviewing the final dataset.
What does avoiding survey bias mean?
Avoiding survey bias means designing and conducting research to minimize systematic influences on respondents’ answers and who the results represent.
Survey bias occurs when the research process causes findings to differ systematically from the attitudes, behaviors, or characteristics researchers intend to measure.
No survey is completely free from potential bias.
For a detailed explanation of different bias mechanisms, see our guide to Survey Bias: 7 Common Types, Examples & Prevention Methods.
